body:
Reply with plain text only, no JSON, no preamble, and do not send messages to anyone else. Do not ask questions; decide.

You are writing short item texts for a Halloween D&D video game, "The Crooked Moon". Each item is a note someone wrote. It needs:
- NAME: a short item name, sentence case (two to five words).
- SUMMARY: one short plain sentence for the inventory, what the thing is, in plain modern English.
- TEXT: the words written on it, in the writer's own voice, under 60 words, signed only if the facts say so.

Rules: our own words. Use only the facts given; invent no new named people, places or history. No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets. Spell correctly.

Output format, nothing else:

ITEM tom_bird_note
NAME: ...
SUMMARY: ...
TEXT: ...

ITEMS:

ITEM tom_bird_note
Facts: a note left in the till of the Hooded Lantern inn in Foxwillow, a burning farm town, by the innkeeper, a reminder to themself: anyone asking about a strange bird should ask Old Tom Crowley in the lanes, who can tell any crow by its eye. Plain, folksy. Unsigned.

ITEM ferryman_copper_note
Facts: a scrap nailed in a tin to a mooring post in Murkwater Bend, a swamp town on stilts: a warning from one boatman to the next that the coffin-boat Ferryman takes copper only, one coin from each of the four districts, the pits, the boathouses, Traders' Row and the Mud Church, and never offer him gold. Sly swamp voice. Unsigned.

ITEM kennel_book_page
Facts: a page from the kennel book at Glitterdeep mining camp: the old miners kept pet centipedes to smell gas, each with a brass collar numbered I to XII; the page lists them with their feeding, each name crossed out over the years, then a thirteenth line, XIII, added late, never crossed out, with "eats more than the rest" beside it. A miner's blunt hand. Unsigned.
result:
ITEM tom_bird_note
NAME: Note from the till
SUMMARY: A reminder note left in the till by the innkeeper of the Hooded Lantern in Foxwillow.
TEXT: If anyone comes in asking after a strange bird, send them down the lanes to Old Tom Crowley. That man can tell any crow just by looking it in the eye.

ITEM ferryman_copper_note
NAME: Warning from the mooring post
SUMMARY: A boatman's warning nailed inside a tin on a mooring post in Murkwater Bend.
TEXT: Listen close if you mean to hail the coffin-boat. The Ferryman takes copper and nothing else. Bring one coin from the pits, one from the boathouses, one from Traders' Row, and one from the Mud Church. Never offer him gold.

ITEM kennel_book_page
NAME: Glitterdeep kennel book page
SUMMARY: A page from the Glitterdeep mining camp kennel book listing the pet centipedes kept to smell gas.
TEXT: Collars I through XII, fed on schedule, each name crossed out over the years as the gas or age took them. Collar XIII, added late at the bottom, never crossed out. Eats more than the rest.
